about.title: Scotts Valley Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Scotts Valley residents often travel to nearby Santa Cruz or San Jose facilities for specialized care, and a mistake at any point in that chain—diagnosis, treatment, or follow-up—can cause lasting harm. Medical malpractice cases are different from most injury claims because California's MICRA law sets strict rules: a short filing window, a required 90-day notice before suing, and a mandatory review by a qualified medical expert to confirm the care fell below an accepted standard. A bad result by itself isn't enough; the law requires proof that a provider's conduct, not just an unfortunate outcome, caused the harm. Our team will review what happened, explain your options under California's specific malpractice rules, and tell you honestly whether you have a claim worth pursuing.

whyChoose.title: What Makes Medical Malpractice Claims in California Different

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day notice before a lawsuit can even be filed. Missing any of these steps can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Mandatory
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, California requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the care given fell below an accepted standard. Our team can help arrange that review early.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But Rising
items.desc: State law places a cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, though that cap increases each year under current law. We can walk you through how this affects your specific situation.

items.question: I think a doctor near Scotts Valley missed something obvious. Is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily — California law requires more than a bad outcome or a missed diagnosis on its own. There has to be evidence the provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful doctor would have done, which is why a qualified medical expert has to review the case. We can help arrange that review to see if your situation meets that standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if the injury happened at a hospital outside Scotts Valley?
items.answer: It doesn't matter which city or county the treatment occurred in — California's rule generally applies statewide: one year from when you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the date of injury. There's also a required 90-day notice before filing suit, so timing matters early on. Our team can pinpoint your exact deadlines once they know the details.
